audit_findings.title: Post-acquisition common equity is valued with a pre-acquisition earnings numerator
audit_findings.magnitude: $424.227 million acquisition consideration; Purchasing Power contributed $237.519 million of revenue and a $7.791 million pre-tax loss in the first six months of 2026; sustainable OE effect unquantified
audit_findings.mechanism: The OE numerator excludes Purchasing Power while the cash, debt and common-equity claim are measured after its acquisition.
audit_findings.evidence: This MD&A does not include, reflect, or give effect to the acquisition of Purchasing Power.
audit_findings.explanation: This is a demonstrated perimeter error. The valuation combines legacy FY2025 earnings with a post-acquisition balance sheet. Purchasing Power's filed 2026 results show that the omitted business is large relative to the $28.7 million anchor, but its sustainable owner earnings could be positive or negative, so the direction is mixed.
audit_findings.action: Rebuild the valuation using post-close consolidated owner earnings or a full pro forma combining legacy PRG and Purchasing Power, including working-capital investment, purchase-accounting effects, integration costs and acquisition financing.

audit_findings.title: Acquisition financing costs are not reflected in anchor OE
audit_findings.magnitude: Filed six-month interest expense increased $13.849 million year over year, including $9.145 million of asset-backed interest, versus the $28.7 million OE anchor; sustainable full-year amount unquantified
audit_findings.mechanism: Equity-level OE must retain interest and funding costs when debt is treated as context only rather than deducted in the equity bridge.
audit_findings.evidence: Purchasing Power also had approximately $338.6 million of non-recourse funding debt under its securitizations and warehouse facilities that remained in place following the acquisition.
audit_findings.explanation: The timing mismatch is demonstrated: FY2025 OE predates acquisition financing, while the post-close bridge does not deduct debt. The six-month increase in interest expense equals 48.3% of the anchor, although part related to temporary borrowings repaid by June 2026. Omitting the sustainable portion overstates value.
audit_findings.action: Reconcile a sustainable full-year post-acquisition interest run rate by debt instrument, including asset-backed funding, commitment fees and lost cash interest, then rerun OE without separately deducting the same debt.

audit_findings.title: Discontinued-operation gains could contaminate the small anchor
audit_findings.magnitude: $22.436 million of filed 2025 discontinued-operation earnings, equal to 78.2% of the $28.7 million anchor
audit_findings.mechanism: Any Vive operating earnings, disposal gains or wind-down effects left in the OE numerator would be capitalized through the forecast and terminal value despite being outside continuing operations.
audit_findings.evidence: Earnings from discontinued operations, net of income tax, amounted to $22.4 million in 2025 and related to the sale of substantially all of Vive's assets.
audit_findings.explanation: Contamination is an unresolved possibility, not a demonstrated error: the filing presents Vive separately, but the supplied record does not show the OE build. The potential amount is nevertheless large enough to be material if it entered the anchor.
audit_findings.action: Trace the $28.7 million OE calculation from its starting income line and document removal of all Vive results, including the $28.5 million portfolio-sale gain, $8.5 million charged-off-receivable gain and related taxes and wind-down costs; confirm sale cash was not also added in the bridge.

audit_findings.title: Multi-year restructuring cannot automatically be stripped as one-off
audit_findings.magnitude: $2.798 million in 2025, equal to 9.7% of the $28.7 million anchor; $44.5 million filed aggregate through 2025 and $3.916 million additional in the first six months of 2026
audit_findings.mechanism: Adding recurring restructuring charges back to OE without a replacement cost raises the anchor and every projected cash flow.
audit_findings.evidence: The Company continued such activities during 2023, 2024 and 2025 and recorded restructuring expenses of $ 2.8 million, $ 20.8 million, and $ 12.5 million for the years ended December 31, 2025, 2024, and 2023, respectively, resulting in aggregate expenses of $ 44.5 million since the inception of the restructuring activities in 2022.
audit_findings.explanation: The recurring pattern is demonstrated, but the record does not establish whether the valuation added these charges back or what sustainable replacement cost is required. The 2025 amount alone is meaningful but does not establish the actual valuation error.
audit_findings.action: Inspect the OE adjustments for restructuring, severance, contract termination and impairments; retain recurring adaptation costs or substitute a supported normalized annual cost, then rerun the valuation if an add-back was used.

audit_findings.title: Charged-off receivable recoveries require symmetric treatment
audit_findings.magnitude: $6.652 million filed 2025 gain, equal to 23.2% of the $28.7 million anchor; $11.158 million of additional filed gains in the first six months of 2026
audit_findings.mechanism: OE is understated if recurring recoveries are removed while related charge-offs remain, but overstated if an unusually high sale gain is treated as a perpetual recovery rate.
audit_findings.evidence: We expect further sales of portfolios to recur on an ongoing basis in 2026 and beyond.
audit_findings.explanation: The treatment in the OE build is unresolved, but the filed gains are material relative to the anchor and recurring sales occurred in 2026. Direction depends on whether provisions, charge-offs, cash recoveries and portfolio-sale proceeds were treated symmetrically.
audit_findings.action: Reconcile provisions, gross charge-offs, ordinary recoveries and sale proceeds by vintage; estimate a sustainable recovery percentage from filed history and rerun OE using that rate consistently.

audit_findings.title: Unidentified D&A is conservatively left in owner earnings
audit_findings.magnitude: $62.0 million identified as residual in FY2020; FY2025 anchor-period amount unquantified
audit_findings.mechanism: Eligible non-economic D&A left as an expense reduces OE; because the valuation uses latest FY2025 OE rather than a trend, only an unsupported residual in the anchor period would directly change value.
audit_findings.evidence: identified eligible D&A is below the filed composite; residual is conservatively left as an expense, not added back: FY2020 $62.0m (2.7% of filed D&A)
audit_findings.explanation: This is a conservative classification uncertainty, not a demonstrated valuation error. The supplied $62.0 million relates to 2020 and therefore does not quantify the effect on the FY2025 anchor. Materiality cannot be established without the anchor-period residual and evidence that it qualifies for add-back.
audit_findings.action: Obtain the FY2025 D&A composition, quantify the residual, and add back only components supported as non-economic and not already captured elsewhere; rerun only for the verified eligible amount.
